subject.title: Feature Request: Surface API provider name in error/overload messages

question: Should transient user-facing provider errors show only provider/model context, or also broader profile/trigger context as proposed by the open linked PR?
rationale: The implementation layer is clear, but the delivered error text appears in shared channels like Telegram and needs a maintained privacy and supportability boundary before landing.

options.title: Land Constrained Transient Context
options.body: Refresh the linked PR or a replacement so overloaded/rate-limit messages include active provider/model and only approved safe context such as profile presence.

options.title: Provider-Only Message
options.body: Narrow the fix to the original request by showing the provider name while leaving profile and trigger details out of channel-visible copy.

options.title: Keep Generic Copy
options.body: Leave transient user-facing errors generic and rely on logs or lifecycle metadata for provider diagnosis, accepting the current UX ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Land Constrained Transient Context
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR or a replacement so overloaded/rate-limit messages include active provider/model and only approved safe context such as profile presence.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the broadest history across the formatter, failover, and embedded runner behavior that controls this user-visible path.
